review_notes: Each renderer profile keeps its authentic independent180-clause bank. Their validators preserve original90-rule targets, exact source/codec/exclusion/context bindings and frozen original preprocessing ownership.
No merged360-row bank enters original decoder/count streams. The inherited trainer code, optimizer, selector and source projections are unchanged.

Adopted per-bank caches keep original model/tensor handles and original cache receipts; only paired orders and descriptive receipts are replaced. In-place tensor or frozen-state changes are checked before/after loss/readout.
Alternating global committed t dispatches one role using local floor(t/2). Retried or abandoned forwards do not advance a sampler or create optimizer commits.

Inherited trainer records auxiliary receipts after optimizer.step; reconciliation counts only declared committed_updates and preserves their original records. The prior four-template counter is retained and labelled inapplicable.
Four complete170-step synthetic report controls show255presentations peractualtemplate,510perbank and2–3presentations per source; these are fixture report counts, not actual training results.

Source-vector provenance, native encoder execution, resource/readiness and quality/proof gates remain outside this private adapter. Actual training and all retention panels require separate guarded execution.
limits: This review does not run the inherited full trainer or attest optimizer commits.
Synthetic report controls and inert helper controls do not authenticate real native assets or semantic quality.
Separate numerical controls use explicit synthetic encoder receipts and a tiny decoder; they are not production reconstruction or retained-model improvement evidence.
Adapting dispatch alone does not establish retention across original/normative/new balanced TRAIN panels, exposed development, or untouched holdouts.
Recorded owner pins identify reviewed files, not a complete transitive execution closure.
